summary.en: Born in Norway, Erik Thorvaldsson went to Iceland as a boy when his father was exiled for manslaughter, and was later outlawed from Iceland for killings of his own. He explored southwest Greenland in 982–985 and led the settlers who founded the Norse colony there. According to the sagas he farmed at Brattahlíð until his death soon after 1000.

summary.en: A Breton mariner from Saint-Malo, Cartier made three voyages for Francis I (1534, 1535–36, 1541–42), claiming the Gaspé for France, sailing up the St. Lawrence to the Iroquoian towns of Stadacona and Hochelaga and giving the name "Canada", from the Iroquoian word for village.

story.en:
On his first voyage in 1534 Cartier explored the Gulf of St. Lawrence and at Gaspé met a fishing party of St. Lawrence Iroquoians led by Donnacona. He raised a cross some ten metres (30 feet) high, which Donnacona protested, and then sailed home with two of the chief's sons, Domagaya and Taignoageny.

The young men guided him the next year up the great river to their town of Stadacona, and Cartier pressed on to Hochelaga, a palisaded town of perhaps 1,500 to 3,000 people below a mountain he named Mont Royal. That winter, frozen in near Stadacona, his crews were dying of scurvy until Domagaya showed them how to brew a tea from the bark and needles of a tree, probably white cedar.

Cartier repaid the help by kidnapping Donnacona and nine others to France, where most died. His third voyage, meant to found a colony and find the rich "Kingdom of the Saguenay", came home with quartz and pyrite mistaken for diamonds and gold. When Champlain arrived 60 years later, the St. Lawrence Iroquoian towns had vanished.
story.zh:
1534年第一次远航时，卡蒂埃考察了圣劳伦斯湾，在加斯佩遇到唐纳科纳率领的一支圣劳伦斯易洛魁人捕鱼队伍。他竖起一座约十米高的十字架，唐纳科纳提出抗议，卡蒂埃随后带着酋长的两个儿子多马加亚和泰尼奥阿格尼返航。

次年，两位青年为他领航，沿大河而上来到他们的城镇斯塔达科纳；卡蒂埃又继续前往霍切拉加，那是一座约有一千五百至三千人、围有木栅的城镇，坐落在一座被他命名为“皇家山”的山脚下。那个冬天，船只冻结在斯塔达科纳附近，船员们接连死于坏血病，直到多马加亚教他们用一种树（可能是北美香柏）的树皮和针叶熬茶。

卡蒂埃却以绑架唐纳科纳等十人回法国作为回报，其中大多数人客死异乡。他的第三次远航本意是建立殖民地、寻找富饶的“萨格奈王国”，结果只带回了被误认为钻石和黄金的石英与黄铁矿。六十年后尚普兰到来时，圣劳伦斯易洛魁人的城镇已经消失无踪。

summary.en: Enriched by the conquest of Peru, de Soto led some 600 men on a four-year expedition (1539–43) through the Mississippian chiefdoms of the Southeast, seizing food and porters, fighting the battle of Mabila and becoming the first European to cross the Mississippi. story.en:
La Salle was a former Jesuit novice from Rouen who came to Canada at 23 and became obsessed with the great river the Indigenous nations described to the west. Backed by Governor Frontenac and the king, he built the first sailing ship on the upper Great Lakes, the Griffon, which vanished with its cargo of furs in 1679.

In early 1682, with some two dozen Frenchmen and a smaller party of Abenaki and Mahican allies and their families, he descended the Illinois River and the Mississippi past Quapaw, Taensa and Natchez towns. On 9 April, near the river's three mouths, he raised a cross and a column bearing the king's arms and claimed every land drained by the river, a territory he had barely seen.

Sailing from France in 1684 with four ships and some 320 people, he could not find the delta and in early 1685 landed hundreds of kilometres west, on the Texas coast. Ships were wrecked, disease and Karankawa attacks killed most of the settlers, and on a desperate overland march to find the Mississippi in 1687 his men shot him. The wreck of his ship La Belle was found in Matagorda Bay in 1995.
story.zh:
拉萨勒出身鲁昂，曾是耶稣会初修士，23岁来到加拿大后，对原住民所描述的西方大河魂牵梦萦。在总督弗隆特纳克和国王的支持下，他在五大湖上游建造了第一艘帆船“格里芬”号，该船于1679年满载毛皮失踪。

1682年初，他带着二十多名法国人，以及一支人数稍少的阿贝纳基、马希坎盟友队伍及其家眷，沿伊利诺伊河和密西西比河而下，经过夸帕、坦萨和纳奇兹人的城镇。4月9日，在大河三个入海口附近，他竖起十字架和刻有国王纹章的石柱，宣布占有这条河流所流经的全部土地，而这片土地他几乎从未见过。

1684年他带着四艘船和约320人从法国出发，却找不到三角洲，于1685年初在以西数百公里的得克萨斯海岸登陆。船只失事，疾病和卡兰卡瓦人的袭击夺去了大多数移民的生命；1687年，在一次孤注一掷、从陆路寻找密西西比河的行军中，他被部下枪杀。他的船“美人”号残骸于1995年在马塔戈达湾被发现。

story.en:
Washington was not a brilliant battlefield general; he lost more battles than he won. His genius lay in keeping an army in existence. Through the winter at Valley Forge in 1777–78, when some 2,000 of his men died of disease, he held the Continental Army together and let the Prussian volunteer Baron von Steuben drill it into a professional force.

Twice he gave up power when he could have kept it. In March 1783 at Newburgh, when officers angry over unpaid wages hinted at defying Congress, he fumbled for his spectacles before reading them a letter, remarking that he had grown grey and almost blind in the service of his country; many were moved to tears and the threat faded. That December he resigned his commission to Congress at Annapolis, which astonished Europe; George III reportedly said that if he did so he would be the greatest man in the world.

As president he refused a third term in 1796. He also owned more than 120 enslaved people, and only in his will did he arrange for those he owned to be freed after his wife's death.
story.zh:
华盛顿并不是一位才华横溢的战场将领，他输掉的战役比赢得的还多。他的天才在于让一支军队得以存续。1777至1778年在福吉谷的冬天，他的部下约有两千人死于疾病，但他维系住了大陆军，并让普鲁士志愿者冯·施托伊本男爵把它训练成一支职业军队。

他两度在本可以保有权力的时候放弃了权力。1783年3月在纽堡，因欠饷而愤怒的军官们暗示要对抗国会。华盛顿在宣读一封信之前摸索着戴上眼镜，说自己为国效力已经头发花白、几近失明；许多人感动落泪，兵变的威胁随之消散。同年12月，他在安纳波利斯向国会交还了军权，令欧洲为之震惊；据说乔治三世曾说，如果他真这样做，他将是世界上最伟大的人。

担任总统期间，他在1796年拒绝第三次连任。他也拥有一百二十多名被奴役者，直到立遗嘱时，才安排在妻子去世后释放他名下的奴隶。

story.en:
Tecumseh grew up in a world of war: his father was killed fighting the Virginians in 1774, and his town was burned several times. After the Treaty of Greenville in 1795 ceded most of Ohio, he stayed away from the signing and moved west. His younger brother Lalawethika, a failed medicine man, had a vision in 1805 and became Tenskwatawa, "the Open Door", preaching rejection of alcohol and American ways. Thousands came to hear him at Prophetstown on the Wabash.

Tecumseh turned the religious movement into a political one. When Governor William Henry Harrison bought some three million acres at Fort Wayne in 1809 from leaders Tecumseh considered unauthorised, he confronted Harrison at Vincennes and then travelled south as far as Muscogee country to recruit allies.

In his absence Harrison attacked Prophetstown at Tippecanoe in November 1811. Tecumseh joined the British in 1812 and impressed General Brock, who wrote that no more sagacious or gallant warrior existed. When the British general Procter retreated after Lake Erie, Tecumseh pressed him to turn and fight; at the Thames the British line broke and Tecumseh was killed. Where his remains lie is unknown.
story.zh:
特库姆塞在战火中长大：他的父亲1774年在与弗吉尼亚人作战时阵亡，他的村镇数次被焚。1795年《格林维尔条约》割让了俄亥俄大部分土地，他没有出席签约，后来向西迁徙。他的弟弟拉拉维西卡原是个不成功的巫医，1805年见到异象后改名腾斯克瓦塔瓦，意为“敞开的门”，宣扬拒绝酒精和美国人的生活方式。成千上万的人来到沃巴什河畔的先知镇听他布道。

特库姆塞把这场宗教运动变成了政治运动。1809年，总督威廉·亨利·哈里森在韦恩堡从一些特库姆塞认为无权代表的首领手中买下约三百万英亩土地，特库姆塞在文森斯当面与哈里森对质，随后南下远至马斯科吉人的地域招募盟友。

他不在时，哈里森于1811年11月在蒂珀卡努进攻先知镇。1812年特库姆塞加入英军，令布罗克将军印象深刻，后者写道，再没有比他更睿智、更英勇的战士了。伊利湖战役后英国将军普罗克特撤退，特库姆塞一再敦促他停下迎战；在泰晤士河畔，英军防线崩溃，特库姆塞战死。他的遗骸葬于何处至今不明。

story.en:
Lincoln had less than a year of formal schooling, scattered over his childhood on frontier farms in Kentucky and Indiana. He read borrowed books by firelight, split rails, piloted a flatboat to New Orleans, and taught himself law. In 1858, running for the Senate against Stephen Douglas, he warned that a house divided against itself cannot stand. He lost that race, but the debates made him a national figure.

As president he moved cautiously, first insisting the war was only to save the Union, then using his war powers against slavery. He wrote his own speeches; the Gettysburg Address of about 270 words reframed the war as a new birth of freedom. In his second inaugural, weeks before the end, he spoke of binding up the nation's wounds with malice toward none.

On Good Friday, 14 April 1865, the actor John Wilkes Booth, a Confederate sympathiser, shot him in the back of the head at Ford's Theatre. He died the next morning in a boarding house across the street, and his funeral train largely retraced, in reverse, his 1861 journey from Springfield to Washington.
story.zh:
林肯一生受过的正规教育总共不到一年，零零散散分布在他于肯塔基和印第安纳边疆农场度过的童年里。他在火光下读借来的书，劈过栅栏木，驾平底船到过新奥尔良，并自学法律。1858年他与斯蒂芬·道格拉斯竞选参议员，警告说一座自相分裂的房子是站立不住的。他输掉了那次选举，但辩论使他成为全国知名人物。

作为总统，他行事谨慎，起初坚称战争只是为了保全联邦，后来又运用战时权力打击奴隶制。他亲自撰写讲稿；约270个词的葛底斯堡演说把这场战争重新诠释为自由的新生。在战争结束前几周的第二次就职演说中，他呼吁不怀恶意地包扎国家的创伤。

1865年4月14日耶稣受难日，同情南方的演员约翰·威尔克斯·布斯在福特剧院从背后枪击林肯头部。林肯于次日早晨在街对面的一所寄宿公寓中去世，他的灵柩列车大体沿着1861年他从斯普林菲尔德前往华盛顿的路线逆向返回。

story.en:
King was 26 and new to Montgomery when he was drafted to lead the bus boycott, partly because he had not yet made enemies. In January 1956, after his house was bombed and an angry crowd gathered with guns, he stood on the porch and asked them to go home and meet hate with love. Influenced by Gandhi and by Christian theology, he made disciplined nonviolence the movement's method.

In Birmingham in April 1963 he was jailed for defying an injunction and, on the margins of a newspaper, wrote a reply to white clergymen who had called the protests untimely, arguing that people who wait for justice are told to wait for ever. Weeks later the city's use of hoses and dogs on marching children turned national opinion.

In his last years he turned to poverty and opposed the Vietnam War, alienating allies in the White House. He went to Memphis in 1968 to support striking sanitation workers. The night before his death he told an audience that he had seen the promised land, though he might not get there with them. He was shot on the motel balcony the next evening, 4 April.
story.zh:
金26岁刚到蒙哥马利时，被推举领导公交车抵制运动，部分原因是他还没有树敌。1956年1月，他的住宅被炸，愤怒的人群持枪聚集，他站在门廊上请大家回家，以爱回应仇恨。受甘地和基督教神学的影响，他把有纪律的非暴力确立为运动的方法。

1963年4月在伯明翰，他因违抗禁令入狱，在报纸页边空白处给那些称抗议“不合时宜”的白人牧师写了回信，指出那些等待正义的人总是被告知要永远等下去。几周后，该市用消防水龙和警犬对付游行儿童，扭转了全国舆论。

晚年他转而关注贫困问题，并反对越南战争，与白宫的盟友渐行渐远。1968年他前往孟菲斯声援罢工的环卫工人。遇害前夜，他对听众说，他已经看到了应许之地，尽管他也许无法与他们一同抵达。第二天傍晚，4月4日，他在汽车旅馆的阳台上中弹身亡。

He introduced official bilingualism and multiculturalism, invoked the War Measures Act in 1970, defeated the 1980 sovereignty referendum and patriated the constitution with the Charter of Rights.

summary.en: Born in Greenland to a Danish pastor and a Greenlandic mother and fluent in Kalaallisut, Rasmussen founded the trading station of Thule in 1910 and led seven Thule Expeditions. story.en:
Rasmussen grew up among Greenlandic children at Ilulissat, learning to drive dogs and hunt, and he thought of himself as part Greenlander all his life. In 1910, with the explorer Peter Freuchen, he set up a trading post among the Inughuit, the northernmost Inuit, and named it Thule; its profits paid for his expeditions.

The Fifth Thule Expedition was his great work. From a base near Hudson Bay a team of Danish scientists and Greenlandic hunters studied the Inuit of the central Arctic; then in 1923 Rasmussen set off westward with two Inughuit companions, Arnarulunnguaq and Qaavigarsuaq, travelling by dog sled for some sixteen months across Arctic Canada to Alaska. Because he spoke Kalaallisut, he could make himself understood by the Inuit groups he met, showing how closely related Inuit languages and cultures were from Greenland to the Bering Strait.

He collected thousands of songs, myths and shamanic teachings, including the words of the Iglulik shaman Aua. Arnarulunnguaq, the only woman on the sled journey west, is now recognised as a pioneer in her own right.
story.zh:
拉斯穆森在伊卢利萨特的格陵兰孩子中间长大，学会了驾驭狗拉雪橇和狩猎，终生认为自己有一部分是格陵兰人。1910年，他与探险家彼得·弗洛伊肯在最北端的因纽特人群体因纽古伊特人中间建立了一个贸易站，命名为“图勒”，其利润用来资助他的探险。

第五次图勒探险是他的代表作。由丹麦科学家和格陵兰猎人组成的团队以哈德逊湾附近为基地，研究北极中部的因纽特人；1923年，拉斯穆森带着两位因纽古伊特同伴阿纳鲁伦瓜克和卡维加尔苏瓦克向西出发，乘狗拉雪橇历时约十六个月，横越加拿大北极地区直抵阿拉斯加。由于他会说格陵兰语，他能与沿途遇到的因纽特群体沟通，显示出从格陵兰到白令海峡的因纽特语言和文化彼此关系密切。

他收集了数以千计的歌谣、神话和萨满教诲，其中包括伊格卢利克萨满奥阿的话语。西行雪橇之旅中唯一的女性阿纳鲁伦瓜克，如今被公认为一位独立的先驱。

summary.en: A Scottish-born partner in the North West Company, Mackenzie followed the Dehcho, now the Mackenzie River, to the Arctic Ocean in 1789, and in 1793 crossed the Rockies to the Pacific near Bella Coola with Indigenous guides, the first recorded crossing of North America north of Mexico.
